titre: The Plaster Froze the Bodies, and Our Assumptions Along With Them
accroche: The Pompeii casts tell stories of families. In 2024, DNA refuted most of them
contenu_vulgarise:
The bodies of Vesuvius's victims were not preserved. What was preserved is their absence.

The ash that fell on Pompeii in 79 hardened around the bodies. The flesh decomposed, leaving within the mass a cavity that matches the body's shape exactly, down to the folds of the clothing and the hairstyle. The bones stayed inside.

## Fiorelli's idea

For decades, excavators cross these voids without understanding them. They come upon scattered bones in a hollow and move on.

In 1863, Giuseppe Fiorelli, who is then directing the dig, reasons the other way around. The cavity is not an accident of the terrain. It is a mold. He has liquid plaster poured in through an opening, lets it set, then clears away the shell of ash.

Out comes a human form, with its posture, its hands, the fabric clinging to the legs. More than a thousand victims have been recovered this way.

The gesture is a methodological turning point. Fiorelli does archaeology on the void left by a vanished object. He obtains, literally, what conventional excavation would have destroyed.

## What the casts then told

These forms invite a story, and the story came. An adult wearing a gold bracelet, a child on the lap: a mother and her son. Two bodies entwined: two sisters, or a mother and her daughter. A family of four, caught together.

These readings circulated for more than a century, in guidebooks, textbooks, and museum wall labels.

## What DNA refuted

In 2024, a team extracts DNA from bone fragments left caught in the plaster of five individuals, and compares it.

The adult with the gold bracelet is a man, and he is no relation to the child lying on him. The four bodies from the same house, taken for a family, are all men and all unrelated to one another. Of the two entwined bodies, described as two women, at least one is a man.

None of these results says who these people were or what bound them. A bond can be strong without being genetic. They say only that the stories handed down rested on nothing but what seemed obvious: a piece of jewelry, a posture, a closeness.

Fiorelli had found a way to fix a form that excavation would have erased. What the plaster has preserved, besides the bodies, is the assumptions of those who looked at them.

repere.texte: DNA extracted in 2024 from bones caught in the plaster shows that the adult with the gold bracelet, long described as the mother of the child lying on his lap, was a man unrelated to him.
repere.source: Pilli, Vai, Moses et al., “Ancient DNA challenges prevailing interpretations of the Pompeii plaster casts,” Current Biology, 2024

carte.punch: Pompeii's plaster froze the bodies, and the assumptions of those who looked at them.
carte.idee: In 1863, Fiorelli pours plaster into the cavities left by the bodies and recovers whole forms. A century and a half of family stories attached themselves to them. In 2024, DNA refuted them one by one.

pour_aller_plus_loin.titre: Pilli et al. (2024) — Ancient DNA challenges prevailing interpretations of the Pompeii plaster casts
pour_aller_plus_loin.note: In English, open access on PubMed Central; the discussion can be read without any background in genetics.

quiz.question: What did the family stories attached to the casts rest on?
choix: On what posture and jewelry seemed to indicate, and nothing else
On inscriptions found near the bodies in the houses
On analysis of the bones preserved inside the casts
On Roman administrative records listing the inhabitants
quiz.explication: No written source or examination of the bones supported these readings: a bracelet, a child on a lap, two bodies close together were enough to reach a conclusion. That is precisely what the 2024 DNA undid, without saying what bound these people. A bond can be strong without being genetic.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What method does Giuseppe Fiorelli invent in 1863 to recover the bodies of Pompeii's victims?
choix: He photographs the cavities before filling them with transparent resin
He casts the skeletons found in the ash directly
He pours liquid plaster into the cavities left by the vanished bodies
He reconstructs the bodies from drawings made by the first excavators
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Fiorelli realizes that the cavity left by a decomposed body is a mold. He pours liquid plaster into it, lets it set, then clears away the shell of ash to reveal the human form.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What did the 2024 DNA analysis reveal about the four bodies found together in one house, long taken for a family?
choix: They were all men, unrelated to one another
They did form a family, but with no blood tie to the child
They were all women of the same extended family
They belonged to four distinct but neighboring families
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The four bodies from the same house, taken for a family for more than a century, turn out to be all men and all strangers to one another, with no kinship at all.

quiz_supplementaire.question: According to the article, what do the 2024 DNA results actually say?
choix: That no bond, even a nongenetic one, existed between the victims
That the stories handed down rested on nothing but appearances
That Fiorelli was wrong about the identity of all the victims
That the casts themselves were fakes made in the 19th century
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The results do not say who these people were or what bound them, since a bond can be strong without being genetic. They say only that the stories rested on what seemed obvious: a piece of jewelry, a posture.
